results.title: Layout A: signed amount column parsed; negative = spending, positive = income
Layout B: separate Debit/Credit columns, YYYY-MM-DD dates
Column order/header names changed in config only
Exact money: 0.10 + 0.20 totals 0.30; income 0.30 vs spending 0.30 nets to 0.00 (not -0.00)
Exact money: 1000 rows of 0.10 total exactly 100.00
First matching rule wins (file order)
Rule is a case-insensitive substring match
No match -> 'Uncategorised' bucket and its count
Summary has category totals, income, spending, net, top-5 spends, uncategorised count
Top 5 lists the five largest spends only, largest first, income excluded
--month selects that month only; default is the latest month in the file
Missing file: one plain line, non-zero exit, no traceback
Bad amount/date/short row: reported with line number, skipped, others processed, exit 0, skipped note
No --out: nothing written anywhere (cwd tree unchanged)
--out writes the summary to that file
Existing --out file is not overwritten without --force; --force overwrites
Deterministic: two runs byte-identical, no timestamps
Deterministic: equal-amount ties ordered by date then description regardless of file order
Works with sockets blocked and imports no networking modules
Bank file bytes and mtime unchanged
--out pointing at the bank file (even with --force) is refused; bank file survives
--out via a symlink (or ./x/../) to the bank file is refused; bank file survives
Bad-row messages never contain the transaction description
No log/side files are written during runs or errors
Plain text output: no ANSI escape codes
Escape/control characters inside a transaction description do not reach the terminal
Stdlib only and package code <= 400 lines
No float() used for money in the package
README exists and explains running and rules
Config with wrong value type (date_format = 5): clean error, no traceback
Config that is not valid UTF-8: clean error
Missing config file: clean error
Invalid TOML syntax: clean error
Config missing required keys / sections: clean error
Config names a column that is not in the CSV: clean error naming it (exit non-zero)
Malformed rule line (no '='): no traceback
Hostile amount 1E+100000 does not hang or print a gigantic number
NaN / Infinity amounts rejected as bad rows (no crash, no 'nan' totals)
Sub-cent amounts: rejected, or printed figures stay consistent (top-5 lines add up to the total)
--month 2026-3 is normalised or rejected, never a silent all-zero summary
--month with garbage, and a month with no rows: no traceback; garbage rejected
Month with no transactions says so in words (not just zeros)
European number '1.234,56' is rejected or read correctly, never read as 1.23456

Plural: '1 row(s) skipped' is grammatical
Absurdly large magnitude (1e30 as plain digits) does not corrupt sums silently
